title: Jay-Z Will Finally Sing at the Super Bowl Halftime Show
summary:
Rapper Jay-Z will sing at the Super Bowl halftime show in February, the NFL has announced. It will be his first time singing at the big game, even though his company, Roc Nation, has made the halftime show since 2019 and he has helped pick each year's singer.

Super Bowl LXI will take place on February 14 near Los Angeles. Jay-Z will follow recent halftime stars like Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.

The news came after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, sang two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played. They were part of a tour celebrating 30 years since his first album, Reasonable Doubt.

Jay-Z called the journey from Reasonable Doubt to the Super Bowl stage a dream come true. Roger Goodell, the NFL commissioner, said he could not be more excited for fans to enjoy Jay-Z's artistry and cultural impact. He added that his one request when the NFL first worked with Roc Nation was for Jay-Z to sing on stage himself one day.
why_it_matters: It shows how working toward a dream can lead to a big moment you once only hoped for.
